text_version.note: Decreto Supremo N.º 115-2025-PCM (4 articles, single final provision, single repealing provision) and the annexed Reglamento of Law 31814 (6 titles, 36 articles, 6 complementary final provisions). The exposición de motivos and the regulatory impact analysis file are not included. Provision IDs: 'Decreto' = the approving decree; 'Reglamento' = the annexed regulation; DCF = Disposición Complementaria Final.

summary.short: Regulation of Peru's AI Law 31814. Classifies AI uses as prohibited ('uso indebido'), high-risk or acceptable-risk, and sets transparency, human-oversight, record-keeping, impact-assessment and security duties for public entities and private developers and implementers, phased in from 1 to 4 years after September 2025 by entity type, sector and firm size.
summary.long: The Reglamento applies to public administration entities, state-owned companies and private-sector, civil-society and academic actors in the National Digital Transformation System; personal use is excluded, and defence and national-security uses are excluded if they meet listed principles. The PCM, through the SGTD, is the national technical-normative authority: it issues guidelines and binding interpretive opinions, monitors prohibited and high-risk uses, supervises compliance and refers breaches to competent authorities. Six uses are prohibited, including manipulative influence, autonomous lethal capability in the civil sphere, mass surveillance without legal basis, biometric inference of sensitive traits, real-time biometric identification in public spaces (with exceptions for authentication and serious-crime investigation) and predictive profiling of individuals for crime. High-risk uses (critical infrastructure, education, employment, social programmes, credit, health) trigger algorithmic transparency and human oversight. Public entities must also adopt an AI policy, use NTP-ISO/IEC 42001:2025, run security audits and mandatory impact assessments, and publish publicly funded source code; for private actors impact assessments are voluntary, with three-year retention of documentation. The text sets no penalties of its own; it refers to the Comptroller, data-protection law and other authorities. It enters into force 90 business days after publication on 9 September 2025.

obligations.summary: AI systems intended for any of the six listed 'uso indebido' purposes are prohibited: manipulative or deceptive influence on decisions; autonomous lethal capability in the civil sphere; mass surveillance without legal basis or with disproportionate impact; biometric inference of sensitive traits or discriminatory classification; real-time biometric identification for categorisation in public spaces (except identity authentication and preliminary investigation of listed serious crimes); and predicting that a person will commit a crime from profiling.
obligations.applies_from: entry into force of the Decreto (90 business days after publication on 2025-09-09)

evidence.quote: Un sistema basado en IA, se considera de uso indebido, y por ende prohibido, cuando es destinado para

obligations.summary: Implementers (who integrate or deploy AI systems) may not use AI systems for the six prohibited 'uso indebido' purposes of Art. 23.1(a)-(f); AI supporting human assessment of a person's involvement in an existing criminal activity, based on objective facts and with oversight, is not considered prohibited (Art. 23.4).
obligations.applies_from: entry into force of the Decreto (90 business days after publication on 2025-09-09)

evidence.quote: Todo sistema basado en IA, que se use para impactar de manera irreversible, significativa y negativa en los derechos fundamentales o el bienestar de las personas, bajo cualquier circunstancia, por lo que dicho uso deviene en prohibido.

obligations.summary: Developers of high-risk AI systems must set up algorithmic-transparency mechanisms informing users in advance of the system's purpose, main functions and types of decisions (respecting trade secrets); mechanisms may include visible labelling; decisions impacting human rights must be explainable to affected users (Art. 25.3).
obligations.applies_from: phased for private developers: 1-4 years from 2025-09-10 by sector, 2-3 years for small and micro enterprises (Primera DCF); for public entities see the government_agency row

evidence.quote: El desarrollador o implementador de un sistema basado en IA de riesgo alto debe establecer mecanismos para garantizar la transparencia algorítmica, permitiendo informar al usuario, de forma previa, clara y sencilla

obligations.summary: Implementers of high-risk AI systems must set up the same algorithmic-transparency mechanisms (prior, clear information to users on purpose, main functions and types of decisions; optional visible labelling; explanation of decisions impacting human rights).
obligations.applies_from: phased for private implementers: 1-4 years from 2025-09-10 by sector, 2-3 years for small and micro enterprises (Primera DCF)

evidence.quote: En caso de que, el sistema tome decisiones que impacten en derechos humanos, debe garantizarse la explicación de sus resultados a los usuarios afectados

obligations.summary: Public entities that develop or implement high-risk AI systems must implement the Art. 25 algorithmic-transparency mechanisms on the public-entity schedule.
obligations.applies_from: phased by entity type: 1 year (branches of state, constitutional bodies), 2 years (EsSalud, regional governments, public universities, public companies, other entities), 3 years (local governments Types A-C) from 2025-09-10; optional for local governments Types D-G (Primera DCF)

notes: Numbering: Art. 24.1 lists items a), b), e), f), g), h), i), j); items c) and d) do not appear in the published text, which is annotated as published. Art. 24.1(i) also runs a second sentence on inferring emotions in workplaces and educational centres (except for medical or safety reasons) into the health item without a separate letter. Timing: the general entry into force is 90 business days after publication (calendar date not computed here), but Reglamento DCF Primera, Segunda, Cuarta and Quinta took effect on 2025-09-10, and all phase-in periods count from 2025-09-10. The phased schedule covers only Art. 25 and Title VI (Chapter I for public entities, Chapter II for private developers and implementers); the prohibitions (Art. 23), Sexta DCF and other provisions apply from general entry into force. Phase-in dates are coded at month precision. For local governments Types D-G, implementation of Art. 25 and Title VI Chapter I is optional according to their resources and capacities. The text does not say whether the small and micro enterprise schedule or the sectoral schedule prevails for a firm covered by both; medium enterprises are not given a separate schedule. The Primera DCF uses 'MYPES' (micro and small enterprises), while Art. 18 uses 'MIPYME'. Private-sector high-risk impact assessments are voluntary (Art. 32.1); for public entities they are mandatory (Art. 30.1). Defence and national-security uses are excluded from scope only if they meet listed principles (Art. 4(b)).
